additions.description: Private user creation endpoint accepts and persists caller-supplied is_active and is_superuser fields.
additions.reasoning: The specification requires that superusers can create users and verifies returned email/id/is_active, but it does not require the API to allow clients to set privilege or activation flags during creation. Exposing is_active and is_superuser in POST /api/v1/users/ is additional behavior.

additions.description: Superuser update-by-id endpoint allows changing is_active and is_superuser on existing users.
additions.reasoning: The specification requires updating a user's email/full_name by id and checking duplicate/nonexistent cases, but it does not require support for modifying activation status or superuser status. PATCH /api/v1/users/{user_id} implementing these fields is extra functionality.

additions.description: Non-superusers can list their own items via GET /api/v1/items/.
additions.reasoning: The specification explicitly tests item listing only for a superuser and does not positively require normal users to have a filtered self-only list endpoint. Returning only the caller's items for normal users is an addition beyond the stated requirements.

omissions.reasoning: The specification requires requesting a password recovery email via POST /api/v1/password-recovery/{email}, including 200 success and 404 for nonexistent users. No such route exists.
The specification requires a reset-password operation that accepts token and new_password, returns 200 on success, 400 for invalid token, and 422 for invalid password length. No such route exists.

omissions.description: Missing token test endpoint required by the authentication flows.
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires 'use this access token to call the test token endpoint' and verify it returns the user's email. The code has no such endpoint under /api/v1/.

omissions.description: Password recovery flow is not implemented, including sending recovery email and exposing recovery HTML content.
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires sending a password recovery email verifiable through the mailcatcher service and obtaining password-recovery HTML content for a user's email before resetting the password. The code performs no outbound email interaction and provides no recovery-content endpoint/behavior.

omissions.description: Reset-password token generation, validation, and password update logic are not implemented.
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires generating a reset token, accepting it later, rejecting invalid tokens with 400 detail 'Invalid token', and updating the password so subsequent login with the new password succeeds. The code has no reset-token workflow at all.

omissions.description: Reading a nonexistent user by ID returns the wrong error detail.
omissions.reasoning: For update-by-id on nonexistent users, the code matches the required detail text, but for read user by id the specification elsewhere expects retrieval by id behavior and uses exact messages for not-found cases. The code returns 404 with detail 'User not found', while the explicit required not-found text for nonexistent user-by-id operations is 'The user with this id does not exist in the system' for the by-id user resource family.

omissions.description: Deleting a user does not explicitly ensure that the deleted user's items become inaccessible as required by the user-deletion scenarios.
omissions.reasoning: The specification explicitly requires that after deleting a user—both self-delete and superuser delete—the user's previously created item must return 404 when fetched. The code relies only on ORM relationship cascade on User.items and does not implement or verify deletion of related items in the delete handlers themselves; there is no explicit service logic guaranteeing this required cross-entity effect.
